# A minimal five-fiber tensor dependency need not be homothetic

This is an obstruction to a proposed structural generalization of the
three-fiber rank-one lemma. It does not contradict the polygonization
results already proved, nor OC. It has strictly positive smooth curvature
and an actual convex mixed-integer realization.

## Construction

Let I be a closed normal-angle interval of length less than pi, and choose
a smaller closed interval J inside int(I). Choose a Smith--Volterra closed
nowhere-dense set F in J, containing its endpoints. Let its complementary
open intervals be (a_m,b_m), of lengths l_m. Put

    eta(t)=exp(-1/[t(1-t)]) for 0<t<1, and 0 otherwise,
    phi(theta)=sum_m exp(-1/l_m^2) eta((theta-a_m)/l_m).

The intervals are disjoint. The k-th derivative of each summand is bounded
by C_k l_m^(-k) exp(-1/l_m^2), which tends to zero faster than any power as
l_m->0. Therefore extension by zero across F and outside J is C-infinity.
The function is nonnegative, nonzero, and its zero set within J is exactly
F. Extend it periodically to the normal-angle circle; it is zero near the
ends of I.

Let A=max|phi+phi''| and epsilon=1/(1+4A). For -2<=z<=2 define

    h_z(theta)=1+epsilon (4-z^2)phi(theta).                 (1)

Then

    h_z''+h_z >=1-4 epsilon A=1/(1+4A)>0.

Thus these are smooth support functions of strictly convex bodies K_z,
each containing the unit disk. The family has a genuine convex realization:

    C={(z,x): -2<=z<=2,
         u(theta).x <=1+epsilon(4-z^2)phi(theta)
         for every theta}.

Each displayed inequality is convex in (z,x), since its rearranged left
side is u(theta).x+epsilon z^2 phi(theta). Their intersection is bounded,
closed, convex, and has interior. Its fibers are exactly the K_z of (1).
Take P={-2,-1,0,1,2}.

For any nontrivial anchored representation z=sum_w p_w w, its support gap is

    h_z-sum_w p_w h_w
       =epsilon [sum_w p_w w^2-z^2]phi
       =epsilon Var_p(w) phi.                            (2)

The coefficient is strictly positive. Thus every nontrivial Jensen
constraint is active on F and strict on J\F. None is an identity on I.
No finite subdivision of I into stable equality/strict-gap intervals can
cover these contact transitions.

## The tensor dependency is an irreducible five-point circuit

Since phi vanishes at both endpoints of I, the endpoint harmonic functions
B_z are all the same function B. Write

    f=1-B,      f_z=f+epsilon(4-z^2)phi.

The functions f and phi are independent: phi vanishes on an open interval
inside I where f is strictly negative. They are not proportional.

The representation-preserving space L(P) is exactly span{1,z}: each
neighbor midpoint representation forces every element of L(P) to have zero
second discrete differences. Thus the universal representation-preserving
lift supplies no extra correction coordinates in this example.

In the tensor basis (f,epsilon phi) on the function factor and (1,z) on the
base factor, the five vectors e(z) tensor f_z have coordinates

    (1,4-z^2,z,4z-z^3).                                  (3)

These are an invertible linear recombination of (1,z,z^2,z^3). Any four
rows with distinct z therefore have rank four, by the Vandermonde
determinant. All five rows have rank four. Their unique dependence, up to
scale, is

    (lambda_-2,lambda_-1,lambda_0,lambda_1,lambda_2)
       =(1,-4,6,-4,1).                                   (4)

Indeed the fourth finite difference annihilates each polynomial of degree
at most three. Hence (4) annihilates both sum lambda_z f_z and
sum lambda_z z f_z.

This dependence cannot be decomposed into smaller dependent tensor blocks:
every proper subset of at most four rows is independent. Yet the residual
family has rank two and is not homothetic. In particular, the implication

    tensor-row dependence -> homothetic component

is false beyond the special three-fiber argument. It also fails after
passing to the full representation-preserving universal lift.

## What the example does not exclude

All the support gaps in (2) are multiples of one nonnegative scalar phi.
A correction preserving that scalar cone may still work; the example does
not disprove exact polygonization. It only rules out the stated automatic
homothetic-component classification and a blanket finite stable-arc
partition under smooth positive curvature alone.
